clue.text: Somewhat senseless idea fool holds

indicators.note: the phrase 'idea fool' holds the letters within it, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A dim-witted fool clings to some barely sensible idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' says the letters sit inside 'idEA Fool'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking hearing is missing one of the five senses, so is partly without sense.

clue.text: Former actor cooking a fish, with a little rice

indicators.note: cooking the ingredients works them over into a new arrangement
a little of the rice is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A one-time actor prepares a fish dish with a small side of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' mixes A FISH together with R, the first letter of 'rice' picked out by 'a little'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Sharif, star of Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago, died in 2015, so he is a performer of the past.

clue.text: Stupid, like Patsy

definitions.meaning: the name Patsy is headed by P, the musical symbol for piano or soft, so it is literally led by 'soft'; a patsy is also a dupe

explanation.surface: Someone describes a friend called Patsy as rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: In music P (piano) means soft, so a word beginning with P, like Patsy, has a soft head.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-headed is a standard adjective for foolish or lacking good sense.

clue.text: Was bothered if 30 seconds late, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the spoken sound of the phrase gives the entry

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, so the first half of the word minute, MIN, and late means dead

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they would have been bothered by a half-minute delay.
explanation.walkthrough: MIN (half of 'minute') plus DEAD ('late', as in the late king) is said aloud as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind something is to object to or be troubled by it, so the past tense means was troubled.

clue.text: Strong man, cut out to be a physicist

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
cut means the word man loses its tail letter

explanation.surface: A strongman is cut from the team and ends up a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks 'man' to MA; 'out' rearranges STRONG plus MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Jonas Ångström was a Swedish physicist, remembered in a unit of length.

clue.text: Duck out of kinky sex and drugs

parts.note: S and M, short for sadomasochism
E is ecstasy, so two of them give drugs

explanation.surface: Someone ducks out of a party involving kinky sex and drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck out' looks like a phrase meaning avoid; 'out of' merely links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is a dialect name for a wild duck such as the wigeon or pintail.

clue.text: Hiding away as night's unravelling

indicators.note: unravelling undoes the words so the letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is hidden away as the night comes undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelling' rearranges the letters of AS NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to store it in a secret place, so stashing means concealing.

clue.text: Drug addict's trick cycling

indicators.note: cycling means a letter goes round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or ploy

explanation.surface: A drug addict's dodge involves riding a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the R of RUSE from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is common slang for someone who takes illegal drugs.

clue.text: African playing the piano around lunchtime?

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
playing with the words lets their letters be rearranged

parts.note: one o'clock, lunchtime, is written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa plays the piano around lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges THE PIANO; 'around' wraps that round I, lunchtime taken as one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Ethiopia, a country in the Horn of Africa, is an African.

clue.text: Johnny's so-called friends

definitions.meaning: johnny is British slang for a condom

explanation.surface: Johnny's friends are friends in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnny' looks like a person's name but is British slang for a condom.
explanation.definitionFit: Pals are close companions; the brand name is the other sense.

clue.text: Trees planted at edge of forest by Geoff or Damien

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

indicators.note: the edge of the forest here is its closing letter

explanation.surface: Trees are planted on the edge of a forest by two men named Geoff and Damien.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: a Geoff Hurst (footballer) or a Damien Hirst (artist) is a first-class degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both surnames rhyme with the top grade of British university degree, in rhyming slang.

clue.text: See 25
Gun takes aim, without life being lost

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the aim goes round the next piece

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: lost letters have gone astray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gunman takes aim, with no loss of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: END surrounds FIEL, the letters of LIFE rearranged by 'being lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lee-Enfield was the standard British army rifle, named after the Enfield factory.

clue.text: Use large amounts of RAM following each brief

indicators.note: following puts the ram after the abbreviation

parts.note: ea. is the short form of each
a tup is a ram, an uncastrated male sheep

explanation.surface: A computer program hogs memory with every short task.
explanation.walkthrough: RAM looks like computer memory but is the male sheep, TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up resources is to consume them greedily, devouring a great quantity.

clue.text: Noisy lot dispute "offside"

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument
read as off plus side: off means awry, so the letters of side are rearranged to give this piece

explanation.surface: Rowdy football fans argue over an offside call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offside' splits into 'off' and 'side': 'off' rearranges SIDE to DIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdies are rough, disorderly people, a loud crowd.

clue.text: Finding another 19A worthwhile? Dad is Johnny's alternative

indicators.note: finding another arrangement of the letters signals rearranging them

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, the cash machine abbreviation

explanation.surface: A father, reluctant to use a condom, finds another cash machine worth visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding another' rearranges ATM, WORTHWHILE and DAD together; 'Johnny' is British slang for a condom.
explanation.definitionFit: Coitus interruptus is a contraceptive technique instead of a condom, punning on taking money out.

clue.text: Protest is about money

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A protest is all about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IS to SI; TIN is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a demonstration where protesters occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Returning from French bar, used the Underground

indicators.note: returning means the pair of pieces are read backwards

parts.note: de is French for from
but, as in all but, means except or bar

explanation.surface: Someone back from a French bar took the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses DE plus BUT; the Underground is London's metro, the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: To tube is to travel on the Tube, London's underground railway.

clue.text: Bank of material found in watering holes

indicators.note: found in places the material inside the drinking places

parts.note: bars are pubs, places to drink
clay is a raw material for pottery

explanation.surface: Banks of earthy material line the edges of watering holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank of material' suggests a ridge of earth, but Bank alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barclays is one of Britain's big high-street banks.

clue.text: 15 23 used by 24D 10

indicators.note: used by means employed within the joined answers to 24 down and 10 across

parts.note: the answers to 24 down and 10 across, a residence and friends, joined into one word

explanation.surface: A cash machine is shared by flatmates.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside flAT Mates, the two answers joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine is a way of taking money from the bank, so a withdrawal method.

clue.text: House dance moves in use, regularly added to the mix

indicators.note: moves means the letters are shifted about into a new order
added to the mix means the picked letters are stirred in with the dance's letters
regularly picks every other letter of in use

explanation.surface: House music dance moves are regularly brought into the mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes IUE from 'in use'; 'moves' rearranges those with DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, the house is the audience, as in a full house.

clue.text: Mean to get drunk

explanation.surface: Someone intends to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend, but is the adjective stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both stingy and inebriated are common senses of the same informal adjective.

clue.text: Made a show of old man, er… dad dancing

parts.note: pa, like old man, is an informal word for father

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: An embarrassed child notes how father showed off with his dad dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges ER and DAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to display it ostentatiously, to show it off.

clue.text: Appearing in film, a demanding person sure of success

indicators.note: appearing in signals the letters show up within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A demanding actor appears in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside filM A DEMANding.
explanation.definitionFit: A made man is someone whose success or fortune is assured.

clue.text: See 26
See 15
Sort of milk drunk by European after credit, 19A having been emptied

indicators.note: after puts the European following the credit

parts.note: full is informal for drunk
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: having been emptied means the middle of the cash machine goes

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, the cash machine

explanation.surface: A European drinks milk bought on credit after the cash machine ran dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like it describes the European, but it is the piece FULL; 'having been emptied' is the usual signal for losing a word's insides.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-cream milk is whole milk with none of its fat removed.

clue.text: Residence recently out of bounds

indicators.note: the bounds of the phrase are its end letters, which are taken out

parts.note: of late means recently

explanation.surface: A residence has recently been declared off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of bounds' removes the end letters O and E from OF LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a self-contained home on one floor of a building, an apartment.

clue.text: 19A ready for use next to Boots?

indicators.note: next to sets the two pieces side by side

parts.note: ready, or the readies, is slang for cash
Boots is a British chain of chemists, which dispense medicines; the query flags the example

explanation.surface: A cash machine is ready for use beside a branch of Boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a UK high-street chemist, a dispensing pharmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole-in-the-wall cash machine is also called an automated teller.

clue.text: 19A usage having expanded now

definitions.meaning: in text messages the three letters of 19 across abbreviate a phrase; written out in full they give the entry

explanation.surface: The use of cash machines has grown at present.
explanation.walkthrough: ATM is texting shorthand as well as a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means currently, just as now does.

clue.text: Show what hot young thing shows, after removing the covers

indicators.note: removing the covers strips the outermost letters away

parts.note: a sexpot is a sexually attractive person

explanation.surface: A striptease: what an attractive young person reveals once undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after removing the covers' strips the outer S and T from SEXPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exhibition, a public display or show.

clue.text: Bottomless depths of 9, once no longer popular with Scotsman

indicators.note: no longer means these pieces are removed

parts.note: Abyssinian is the old word for Ethiopian, the answer to 9 across

indicators.note: with joins the Scotsman to the popular piece

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An old-style African is no longer in favour with a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' drops IN and IAN from ABYSSINIAN, the old name for Ethiopian.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm or deep gulf.

clue.text: Silly plan to cut the end off a melon

indicators.note: silly here means foolishly muddled, so the letters are rearranged
the end off means the last letter of cut is dropped

explanation.surface: A daft scheme to trim the end off a melon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end off' trims CUT to CU; 'Silly' rearranges PLAN TO, CU and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloup is a variety of musk melon with orange flesh.
